Class Form

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.swing.ui.Form
@ViewScoped public final class Form extends Object
Binds the input components of a view to properties, validates their values, and tracks whether they changed. Each view has one, which it injects. 
form.bind(nameField, name).check(Rule.required(messages.nameRequired()));
form.bind(ageField, age, Converter.of(Integer::valueOf, String::valueOf, messages.wholeNumber()));

The bindings are two-way. A user change of a component sets its property, and updates the binding's Binding.validation(), valid() and dirty(), synchronously on the EDT, before the change's event returns, so that a command whose enabled reads them, executed right after, sees the new state. A change of a property, which may be set from any thread, updates its component on the EDT, in an update posted as for Ui.bind(java.util.function.Consumer, Observable); the validations that depend on it, and the form's state, are updated before the change returns when it changes on the EDT, such as from a user change of another component or the edit of a table's cell that modifies a tracked list, once the list has released its lock, and in a posted update otherwise. Each change validates the bindings that depend on it once. Changes that a binding makes to its own component, from the property, are not user changes: they don't show errors, and don't set the property.

A rule or a converter that throws, other than a converter rejecting a text, has a bug: the exception goes to the FailureHandler, and its check is Check.Status.UNKNOWN, as are the rules' after a converter's. An Error is not caught.

Every method is called on the EDT, and every subscription it makes belongs to the view's scope.

    • bind

      public Binding<String> bind(JTextComponent field, Property<String> property)
      Binds a text component to a property of its text. The field's text is set from the property now; each change of the document the field has now sets the property to the text; a change of the property sets the text, unless it already equals the value, so that typing is never interrupted and the caret stays in place.
      Parameters:
      field - the text component
      property - the property
      Returns:
      the binding
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalStateException - if the component is already bound

    • bind

      public <T> Binding<T> bind(JTextComponent field, Property<T> property, Converter<T> converter)
      Binds a text component to a property through a converter. The field's text is set from the property, formatted, now; each change of the document the field has now sets the property to the text parsed, unless the converter rejects it, which leaves the property unchanged; a change of the property sets the text, unless it already parses to an equal value, so that typing is never interrupted and the caret stays in place.

      The converter's requirement is the first check of the binding: when the converter rejects the field's text, the check is unmet and the rules' are unknown, since the property doesn't hold the text.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the value
      Parameters:
      field - the text component
      property - the property
      converter - the converter
      Returns:
      the binding
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalStateException - if the component is already bound

    • bind

      public Binding<Boolean> bind(AbstractButton button, Property<Boolean> property)
      Binds a button, such as a check box, a toggle button or a radio button, to a property of its selected state. The button's selected state is set from the property now; an item event sets the property; a change of the property sets the selected state.
      Parameters:
      button - the button
      property - the property
      Returns:
      the binding
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalStateException - if the button is already bound

    • bind

      public <E> Binding<Optional<E>> bind(JComboBox<E> combo, ObservableList<E> items, Function<? super E, String> text, Property<Optional<E>> selection)
      Binds a combo box to an observable list and to a property of its selected item. The combo box shows items, through a new model that follows the list change by change on the EDT, with a renderer showing text of each element, and becomes not editable. Its selection and selection are kept in step, as Ui.bind(javax.swing.JList, ObservableList, Function, Property) keeps a list's: the user's selection sets the property, and a change of the property selects its value, or clears the selection for an empty value or one that isn't in the list, then setting the property to empty; changes of the list keep the selection on the selected element, by tracking its index. Optional.empty() means no selected item.

      The property's baseline is its value once the binding has selected it, which is empty when the value isn't in the list.

      Type Parameters:
      E - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      combo - the combo box
      items - the elements, made by ObservableList.of(Object[]) or ObservableList.copyOf(Collection)
      text - the text of an element
      selection - the selected element, empty when nothing is selected
      Returns:
      the binding
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalStateException - if the combo box is already bound
